method: blind close reading; no .md, rules, scripts or other chapters opened

facts.fact: 伊琳娜（全名 Clara Elise Irène Cahen d’Anvers，与姨母同名，取自希腊和平女神）于 1872 年 9 月 20 日出生在巴黎以西、塞纳河畔布日瓦尔家中租用的那座十八世纪石堡。
facts.quote: Irène—that is, Clara Elise Irène Cahen d’Anvers—was born on September 20, 1872, in her family’s rented eighteenth-century stone castle in Bougival, west of Paris by the river Seine.

facts.fact: 1878 年 11 月下旬，银行世家继承人、艺术评论家夏尔·埃弗吕西（Charles Ephrussi）找上门来，要求观看 Renoir 那幅画着名媛与两个孩子的巨幅室内像（夏尔庞特夫人像）。
facts.quote: In late November 1878, Charles Ephrussi approached artist Renoir seeking to view his enormous portrait of a prominent socialite with her two children.

facts.fact: 1879 年沙龙成为 Renoir 的关键转折点：夏尔庞特像被挂在香榭丽舍宫主厅的显要位置，靠的是夏尔庞特夫人本人四处游说——她认识评委，知道该在谁手上按一把、该对谁低声说出 Renoir 的名字。
facts.quote: As it turned out, the Salon was a critical turning point for Renoir. The Charpentier portrait hung prominently in the main hall of the Palais des Champs-Élysées, well placed by the vigorous lobbying of Madame Charpentier herself, who understood something essential. She knew the jurors. She knew how to press a hand or whisper Renoir’s name.

facts.fact: Renoir 委托一事在 1880 年整个夏天反复酝酿，细节定在路易·卡昂当韦尔固定在 Café de l’Anglais（意大利人大道、喜歌剧院附近）右后方角落的那张常桌；1880 年 7 月 31 日周六正午，伯爵破例不谈金融、只谈印象派艺术，同桌有画家 Bonnat、夏尔之兄 Ignace Ephrussi 与来自 Trieste 的沙龙女主人 Ernesta Stern——此事见于这些食客写给藏家查尔斯·杜东的信，信中称他「我亲爱的印象派者」。
facts.quote:
The discussions about a Renoir commission lingered through the summer of 1880. The details were debated at Louis Cahen d’Anvers’s regular table at the Café de l’Anglais, a celebrated restaurant on the Boulevard des Italiens near the Opéra-Comique. The count usually held court deep at the back right corner at a permanently reserved table, where the stock tips came with the cream of sorrel soup and the soufflé à la reine, covered in silver domes.


But on this Saturday afternoon on July 31 at noon he was not talking finance, but debating Impressionist art. At the table was artist Bonnat, Ignace Ephrussi—Charles’s brother—and Ernesta Stern, a celebrated society salonnière and writer from Trieste, Italy. The menu was scrambled eggs with tomatoes, veal chop with Pommes Nana, roast quail, and Condé peaches for dessert.


This according to correspondence to Charles Deudon, Renoir’s champion and the artist’s confidant, in a letter written by these restaurant diners, who addressed Deudon as “My dear Impressionist.”

facts.fact: 到 1880 年 8 月，Renoir 已被召到卡昂当韦尔府上，赶在时间动她之前画下伊琳娜；这张画成了他时髦的儿童肖像专长的代表作——那两年他一口气画了二十多个男孩女孩。
facts.quote: By August 1880, Renoir had been summoned to the Cahen d’Anvers mansion to paint Irène’s image before time could touch her. It became representative of Renoir’s fashionable specialty of children’s portraits. He painted more than twenty boys and girls in a two-year burst during this period.

facts.fact: 接单时 Renoir 还在伤后复健：1880 年 1 月他在 9 区 35 rue St.-Georges 家附近的结冰街面上滑倒摔断右臂（La Presse 还上了头条），无法再用惯用的右手，遂改用左手作画数月。
facts.quote: He was recovering from a fractured right arm, suffered in January 1880 when he slipped on an icy street near his home on 35 rue St.-Georges in the 9th arrondissement, an accident headlined by La Presse. The newspaper described his treatment, assuring readers that “everything suggests that no complications will arise, and that Mr. Renoir will be able to resume his brushwork in a few weeks.” Suddenly unable to paint with his dominant right hand, Renoir switched to his left for months.

facts.fact: 画完伊琳娜 Renoir 并不收手：他不请自来回到府上，游说再加画两个妹妹，四处碰壁仍不断写信施压（Fanny Ephrussi 1880 年 8 月记道，他托弟弟夏尔写信问 Louise 何时能画 Alice；他还一心想把伊琳娜送进次年的沙龙）。家族于是折中——一幅画、两个女儿：Alice 与 Élisabeth 于 1881 年 2 月在蒙田大道府中并肩坐定，一着玫瑰色、一着蓝色裙子。
facts.quote:
After Renoir finished with Irène, he didn’t let go. He returned to the Cahen d’Anvers mansion uninvited to lobby to paint two more portraits of Irène’s younger sisters. “I’ve made two attempts to see Madame Cahen,” Renoir wrote to an unnamed correspondent. “I have not yet succeeded.” And he didn’t give up when that effort failed. He sent more letters to increase the pressure. Fanny Ephrussi wrote in August 1880 that her brother Charles, the family’s art adviser, received a note from Renoir. “He asked him to kindly write to Louise,” she said, “to find out when he could paint the portrait of Alice.” Renoir, she added, seemed very busy. He had plans. He wanted Irène in next year’s Salon exhibit. And he wanted that badly.


Instead, the Cahen d’Anvers family compromised. One canvas, two daughters. Alice and Élisabeth posed in February 1881, side by side in rose and blue dresses, inside the mansion on Avenue Montaigne.

facts.fact: 1881 年 7 月沙龙一收，Louise 就明确表态对 Alice 与 Élisabeth 的双人像不满；两幅女孩像被撵到楼上佣人区，夫妇至少拖了一年才付款。Renoir 写信向杜东发泄：「至于卡昂当韦尔家那 1,500 法郎，我实在难以下咽。这家人太抠；我受够了犹太人」——这笔钱约合今日 9,500 美元，是当时 Renoir 收到的最高委托之一。
facts.quote:
Despite Renoir’s critical success, after the Salon of 1881 ended in July Louise Cahen d’Anvers made it clear that she was not pleased with the double portrait of Alice and Élisabeth. The portraits of the girls were banished upstairs to the servants’ quarters of their mansion, and the couple delayed payment for at least a year. The tardiness strained Renoir’s artistic relationship with Louis and Louise Cahen d’Anvers. And the artist complained to friends in their circle, writing a letter to Charles Deudon, the collector who had championed Renoir to Louis.


“As for the 1,500 francs from the Cahens, I must tell you I find it hard to swallow. The family is so tight-fisted; I’m done with the Jews,” Renoir told Deudon. In today’s dollars that would amount to about $9,500—one of the highest commissions Renoir received at the time.

supplementary_observations.fact: 埃弗吕西是卡昂当尔夫妇的艺术顾问；Renoir 邀他与另一位藏家、矿业继承人 Charles Deudon（早期印象派支持者「petit bataillon d’amateurs」一员）在 1879 年沙龙开展前私下看画。
supplementary_observations.quote: Renoir invited Ephrussi, the Cahen d’Anvers family art adviser, and another influential collector, Charles Deudon, an heir to a mining fortune who was part of a circle of early Impressionist supporters known as the petit bataillon d’amateurs. They wanted a private viewing before the Charpentier painting was displayed in the spring of 1879 for the annual rite of passage for artists, the Paris Salon.

supplementary_observations.fact: 埃弗吕西此前已在亚洲艺术藏家 Henri Cernuschi 的 Parc Monceau 宅邸把路易·卡昂当韦尔引见给 Renoir；到夏天他又说服自己的姑母及另两位亲属为 Renoir 坐像。
supplementary_observations.quote: Charles Ephrussi had already introduced Louis Cahen d’Anvers to Renoir at the Parc Monceau mansion of Asian art collector Henri Cernuschi. By the summer, Ephrussi had persuaded his aunt and two other relatives to pose for Renoir.

supplementary_observations.fact: 1875 年 Renoir 的画作与 Monet、Sisley、Morisot 等七十二幅印象派作品一起在 Hôtel Drouot 拍卖，全场哄闹到报警；以今日币值只够付房租的 200 到 1,400 美元成交，许多作品还得由受辱的画家自己买回。
supplementary_observations.quote: Just four years earlier, in 1875, his work had been offered for auction at the Hôtel Drouot alongside seventy-two other Impressionist paintings from Monet, Alfred Sisley, and Berthe Morisot. The event had the manic energy of a spectacle—jeers, hecklers, the police called in to settle the crowd. Renoir’s paintings sold for what would now be barely enough to cover rent—$200 to $1,400 in today’s terms—and many had to be bought back by the humiliated artists themselves.

supplementary_observations.fact: 1877 年约五岁的伊琳娜拍了第一张正式肖像照（银扣、深色天鹅绒、一篮花），已侧目向左——那正是 Renoir 三年后要捕捉的目光；这张巴黎工作室的照片是父母把她推向高社交界「以艺术为印章」的第一步。
supplementary_observations.quote: In 1877, when she was about five, Irène posed for her first formal portrait, a photograph in silver buttons and dark velvet and a basket of flowers, like a French Alice in Wonderland.

supplementary_observations.fact: 长男 Robert 此前已穿水手服、系深红绶带，按西班牙画家 Francesc Miralles i Galaup 学院派的社会肖像路子画过油彩像。
supplementary_observations.quote: Their eldest son, Robert, had already posed for an oil portrait in a sailor suit and crimson sash in the controlled academic style of Spanish painter Francesc Miralles i Galaup, who specialized in traditional society portraits.

supplementary_observations.fact: 卡昂当尔夫妇养三个女儿于丝绸蕾丝之中、两个儿子则被赋予责任：长成金融家、缔配合适的婚姻、联姻以扩张横跨欧洲的家族私人 haute banque；孩子们被教导自己是达维德国王王族的后裔。
supplementary_observations.quote: They raised their three daughters in silk and lace and their two sons with a sense of duty: To grow up to be financiers. To forge suitable marriages. To choose partners who would expand the family’s private haute banque business in branches spread across Europe.

supplementary_observations.fact: 拉乌尔·蒙铁菲奥雷（Raoul Montefiore）是伊琳娜的表兄弟兼邻居，年龄几乎与她同出，自认是她最好的童年玩伴；多年后他在阿尔卑斯山中躲避盖世太保时写下回忆：伊琳娜「热爱生活，她也活过了它」。
supplementary_observations.quote: Her cousin and neighbor Raoul Montefiore—almost Irène’s twin in age, and certain that she was his best childhood friend—remembered her in a single, unambiguous sentence: Irène “loved life and she lived it.”

supplementary_observations.fact: 纳粹早在几个月前就把拉乌尔的妻子从十六区的公寓带走送往奥斯维辛；来抓拉乌尔时又抄走了那份记录 Belle Époque 回忆的脆弱文稿。
supplementary_observations.quote: The Nazis had taken his wife months earlier from her apartment in the 16th arrondissement, transporting her to Auschwitz.

supplementary_observations.fact: 父母对双人像看到的是另一回事：年长的 Élisabeth 着蓝、目光近乎成人，手指紧张地揪着裙褶；Alice 着粉、撅嘴、双腿分开，那份随便令父母觉得粗俗（vulgar）。
supplementary_observations.quote: Alice, in pink, looks uncomfortable, her lips pouting and her legs set far apart, a casualness that disturbed her parents, who considered the portrayal vulgar.

supplementary_observations.fact: 艺术史界相传家族讨厌的是伊琳娜那张（法国报纸称其父见了成品大喊「这样的恐怖东西我不会付 500 法郎」，埃弗吕西据说愿意代付），但此说与事实相悖——他们毕竟又委托了第二幅。
supplementary_observations.quote: The legend shared among art historians is that the family disliked the portrait of Irène, but this view was at odds with many facts. They had, after all, commissioned a second portrait. Decades later a French newspaper claimed that when Irène’s father saw the finished painting of Irène he cried out, “I won’t pay 500 francs for such a horror.” His art adviser, Ephrussi, supposedly offered to pay the commission.

supplementary_observations.fact: 更深的真相由伊琳娜的侄子 Gilbert Cahen d’Anvers 提供：1985 年他在大皇宫的 Renoir 展上与妻子 Josefina 并肩看着 Pink and Blue 双人像时透露，真正惹恼伯爵夫妇的是这幅双人像，而非伊琳娜那张。
supplementary_observations.quote: But there was a deeper truth. Gilbert Cahen d’Anvers was Irène’s nephew. And years later, while gazing at the double portrait of Pink and Blue in a 1985 Renoir exhibition at the Grand Palais in Paris with his wife, Josefina, he confided another story. It was actually that portrait that irked the Count and Countess Cahen d’Anvers, not Irène’s picture. To their consternation, Renoir had not captured the ideal image of five-year-old Alice, but a restless child who was not yet tamed for a portrait.

supplementary_observations.fact: 1962 年，八十六岁的 Alice 在香榭丽舍附近自己的沙龙里握着一张该画的四乘六英寸明信片，对记者说：「我那时五岁，坐着让人画无聊透顶。唯一的安慰是穿上了那件我钟爱的爱尔兰蕾丝裙。」
supplementary_observations.quote: Decades later, in 1962, Alice, then eighty-six, sat in the light of her salon near the Champs-Élysées holding a postcard of the painting, the past compressed to four by six inches. She squinted at it and told a journalist, “I was five years old and I found sitting for the painting so boring. My only consolation was getting to wear that Irish lace dress I loved so much.

supplementary_observations.fact: 1881 年 9 月 Renoir 第三次被召，这次要为家族再添一人：伊琳娜最疼的叔叔 Albert Cahen d’Anvers——三十五岁，已脱离银行行当，改以作曲与配法国诗的小歌剧立身，在左岸 118 rue de Grenelle 的十八世纪小楼里办私人音乐会而成名。
supplementary_observations.quote: Yet that same year, in the thinning light of September 1881, Renoir was summoned a third time to fix another member of the Cahen d’Anvers dynasty onto canvas. This time it was Albert Cahen d’Anvers, Irène’s favorite uncle, the one who had drifted from the banking business to compose melodies and operettas set to French poetry. He was thirty-five and something of an abstraction in the family. He had no taste for their universe of yields and arbitrage, instead making his name by hosting private concerts at his eighteenth-century mansion on the Left Bank, the petit villar at 118 rue de Grenelle.

supplementary_observations.fact: Albert 的书信属于十九世纪同性恋男性圈子的庞大通讯网络；密友 Georges Hérelle 是哲学教授，与他同游俄国与法国各地，其日记手稿藏于特鲁瓦的 Médiathèque Jacques-Chirac；圈子自谓「情感共同体」，以植物隐喻与「特别情感」之类绅士暗语行事。
supplementary_observations.quote: Albert’s letters are part of abundant correspondence within a circle of nineteenth-century gay men with secret private lives cultivated through constant letters and discreet gatherings. Among his closest friends was Georges Hérelle, a philosophy professor who traveled with Albert to Russia and through France, and who played a role as a historian and archivist of Belle Époque homosexuality. His private journals, unpublished manuscripts, letters, and voyage logs are preserved at the Médiathèque Jacques-Chirac in Troyes in the Champagne region of France. They called their circle “a community of emotions” and understood that appearances mattered more than truth. The word “homosexuality” did not exist, so Hérelle resorted to botanical metaphors to “your flower,” or might mention “cultivating oleanders,” or simply used a more common gentlemanly code word: “special sentiments.”

supplementary_observations.fact: Le Monde Artiste 在 1903 年 Albert 的讣告里暗示了他的双重生活：他在法国南部因一场常规手术的并发症猝然去世，享年五十七岁。
supplementary_observations.quote: Le Monde Artiste hinted years later at Albert’s double life in his 1903 newspaper obituary after his unexpected death from complications of routine surgery at the age of fifty-seven in the south of France.

supplementary_observations.fact: 1881 年 5 月 1 日，Renoir 把伊琳娜像与姐妹双人像一起送进香榭丽舍宫工业宫的沙龙——当时欧洲最大的当代艺术展；为保全伊琳娜的匿名，标题只写 Portrait de Mlle.。
supplementary_observations.quote:
Then, on May 1, 1881, Renoir sent Irène’s picture, and the painting of her sisters, into the world for the most public display. The Salon was the kind of place people still believed in then, an annual ritual that drew hundreds of thousands to the Palais de l’Industrie on the Champs-Élysées. Under that vast iron and glass roof—housing the largest exhibition of contemporary art in Europe—reputations were made or quietly erased. Renoir participated because the jurors handed out the medals, because the critics took notes in the margins of their catalogs, because the collectors circulated through the aisles with the certainty that taste could be bought and sold. Women herded their children past the canvases, lingered in front of the Renoir portraits, and exchanged low remarks about brushwork, according to an eavesdropping critic.


Irène’s portrait was one they stopped for. The one that made them hesitate in the vast halls subdivided by iron columns and trusses. Renoir was careful to maintain her anonymity, titling it Portrait de Mlle.

supplementary_observations.fact: 沙龙评审团仍对这两幅卡昂当韦尔女孩像不屑；Renoir 最终从未从偏学术或写实风格的任一届评审团拿到沙龙奖章——那一年奖章给了年仅二十五岁的 John Singer Sargent（二等勋章），而落选的 Pailleron 家父亲 Édouard 大闹评审团。
supplementary_observations.quote: Still, the Salon’s jury scorned the two portraits of the Cahen d’Anvers girls. Ultimately, Renoir never received a Salon award from any of the juries that favored academic or realist styles.

supplementary_observations.fact: Renoir 自己也放心不下：两幅女孩像（1881 年 2 月完成，比画 Albert 早七个月）一收尾他便去阿尔及利亚走了六周，写信给一位藏家说自己累到「连那幅画好坏都说不清」；在埃弗吕西敦促下他仍特地刻了一幅近似版画送进《Gazette des Beaux-Arts》的沙龙评述以推介伊琳娜像，尽管该刊评论员并未说它好话。
supplementary_observations.quote:
Still, Renoir had doubts about the picture of young Alice and Élisabeth, which he completed in February 1881, seven months before he painted Albert’s portrait. He traveled soon after to Algeria for a six-week trip and confided his fears in a letter to a collector: “I left immediately upon finishing the portraits of the little Cahen girls, so tired that I can’t even tell you whether the painting is good or bad.”


In the end Renoir decided he liked the painting of the two sisters. Or liked it enough. With Ephrussi’s urging, Renoir also made a special effort to promote Irène’s portrait, creating a similar etching to be included in the Gazette des Beaux-Arts’s Salon review even though the journal’s art critic had not said anything in the portrait’s favor.

supplementary_observations.fact: Degas 曾在沙龙之后私下指责 Renoir：「Renoir 先生，你没有骨气。为人定制绘画是不可接受的。我听说你现在专为金融家作画。」
supplementary_observations.quote: Artist Edgar Degas, precise and uncompromising, had told him—almost with pity—that painting portraits for wealthy bankers meant surrender. “Monsieur Renoir, you have no integrity. It is unacceptable that you paint to order. I gather you now work for financiers.”

supplementary_observations.fact: 伊琳娜的嫂子、Robert 之妻 Sonia Cahen d’Anvers 在 1972 年自费出版的回忆录里写：这些画被收在她所称的「lumber room」（杂物间）；另有二十世纪中期的艺术史家称双人像被塞进布草间，或在 Avenue Foch 某处六层无电梯的佣人房（chambre de bonne）中被找到。
supplementary_observations.quote: In her privately published memoirs, Irène’s sister-in-law, Sonia Cahen d’Anvers, Robert’s wife, wrote in 1972 that the portraits were kept in what she called—with a kind of brittle English elegance—the “lumber room.” That phrase said everything about a space for things too valuable to throw away, a place crowded with outgrown chairs and odds and ends. Some art historians in the mid-twentieth century passed other stories, claiming that the double portrait of Alice and Élisabeth was banished to linen rooms or ultimately found in a sixth-floor walk-up or a chambre de bonne—a maid’s cramped quarters under a rooftop—on Avenue Foch.

supplementary_observations.fact: Alice 晚年解释说父母其实守旧（他们在沙龙木护墙上挂的是 Nattier 的水泽仙女与 Bonnat 的肖像），而她自己对双人像的下场另有记忆：母亲「后来把它捐给慈善机构，就处理掉了」。
supplementary_observations.quote: Late in life, Alice Cahen d’Anvers tried to explain her family’s preferences. “My parents were very conventional—they hung on the wooden paneling of their salons the Nattier nymphs and Bonnat portraits.” Alice had a different memory of the double portrait’s temporary fate. That her mother “got rid of it later by donating it to a charity.”

supplementary_observations.fact: Josefina 在 2025 年于十六区一条私人门禁街道的公寓里回忆亡夫 Gilbert 的记忆：Renoir 一年受邀来访一次，家里就把画从楼上取下来、摆到显要位置，好让画家对自己画的东西满意。
supplementary_observations.quote: According to Josefina, “when Renoir came to visit—which he was invited to do once a year—they would bring the portraits down from upstairs and put them in a place of honor so that the painter would be pleased with what he had done.”

supplementary_observations.fact: Renoir 对犹太人的敌意在 1890 年代随法国政治转向防御、民族主义与排外而加剧；但其子 Jean 后来写道，父亲把伊琳娜的叔叔 Albert 视作朋友。
supplementary_observations.quote: Renoir’s hostility toward Jews intensified throughout the 1890s as French politics shifted to become more defensive, nationalistic, and xenophobic. Yet his son Jean would later write that his father considered Irène’s uncle, Albert Cahen d’Anvers, a friend.

supplementary_observations.fact: 户口统计显示，巴黎的犹太社区二十年几乎翻倍：从 1872 年约两万五千人增至 1891 年超过四万四千人。
supplementary_observations.quote: Census records show that the Jewish community almost doubled in two decades, increasing from about twenty-five thousand in 1872 to more than forty-four thousand in 1891.

supplementary_observations.fact: 同样被划界的是「Israelites」与「Juifs de l’Est」：卡昂当韦尔这类人家自称 Israelites，同化、住第八区、门上不挂 mezuzah；来自东方、说意第绪语的 Juifs de l’Est 则被视作异类，他们自 1880 年代为躲避 pogrom 而来，相信法国是自由之地、犹太人安全。
supplementary_observations.quote: The family’s members preferred to call themselves Israelites. A Juif was something else—something Eastern, something loud and foreign and too much. Their worlds were circumscribed. Israelites were assimilated and lived in the 8th arrondissement. Israelites did not hang mezuzahs on their doors. They belonged. The fissures were wide between the Israelites and the Juifs de l’Est, the ones who came from the east speaking Yiddish. The tailors and tinkerers and clock peddlers. They prayed the old prayers. They didn’t assimilate. Some were leftists. They started arriving in the 1880s, fleeing the pogroms and believing, as well, that France was the land of liberty, that Jews were safe.

supplementary_observations.fact: 父母当年在 99 Eaton Square（伦敦 Belgravia）躲避战乱，两年后回法，伊琳娜遂生于布日瓦尔的文艺复兴城堡 La Jonchère；伊琳娜的私人教师 Monsieur Rousseau 带着 1870 年普法战争与巴黎公社的血痕，出门必带左轮手枪与 20 法郎——约合今 40 美元、够粗粝地过一周。
supplementary_observations.quote: Many of the family’s servants played memorable roles in Irène’s education, among them her private tutor, known to the children simply as Monsieur Rousseau. He was still scarred by his experiences during the Franco-Prussian War of 1870 and the bloody assault on the Paris Commune. Irène’s own parents had escaped the miseries of war by fleeing to live at 99 Eaton Square in the prestigious London neighborhood of Belgravia. They returned two years later to France, where Irène was born in the Renaissance castle of La Jonchère in Bougival. Once she was old enough to begin a formal education, it was Monsieur Rousseau who watched over her reading. But he also delivered an unspoken lesson. The revolver he carried was as essential to him as a pocket watch. He could not forget the odor of gunpowder and desperation from the Franco-Prussian War. He never left home without it, along with 20 francs—roughly $40 in today’s money, or enough for a week of rough living—in case of a wartime threat.

supplementary_observations.fact: 本章收尾的判语：这一整套画面与规矩是要把伊琳娜准备妥当——一场她并未选择的婚姻，让她在一个已开始把她除名的世界里充当「归属」的标记。
supplementary_observations.quote: And so Irène became part of the story they needed her to tell. They were preparing her, quite methodically, for a marriage she had not chosen. To become an emblem of belonging in a world that was already writing her out.

relationships: Count Louis Cahen d’Anvers——伊琳娜之父，伯爵、银行家，家族私人 haute banque 之主；在 Café de l’Anglais 固定坐右后方那张常桌。
Countess Louise Cahen d’Anvers——伊琳娜之母，生于今意大利 Trieste；Titian 色姜黄金发由此遗传给伊琳娜；1880 年由 Carolus-Duran 画过裸肩像；1881 年 7 月明确表达对双人像的不满。
Irène（Clara Elise Irène Cahen d’Anvers）——本章主角，1872 年 9 月 20 日生，Renoir 笔下《小伊琳娜》的坐像者。
maternal aunt Irène——伊琳娜姨母，名字来源（希腊和平女神 Eirene）。
Robert Cahen d’Anvers——长男，早先由 Francesc Miralles i Galaup 画过水手服油彩像；其妻 Sonia Cahen d’Anvers＝伊琳娜的嫂子，1972 年回忆录里提到「lumber room」。
Alice Cahen d’Anvers——三姐妹中最小、最严肃者，1881 年 2 月与 Élisabeth 同幅（粉裙）时年五岁，1962 年八十六岁受访；拉乌尔童年「想娶」的就是她。
Élisabeth Cahen d’Anvers——较 Alice 年长，双人像中着蓝。
Albert Cahen d’Anvers——伊琳娜最喜爱的叔叔，三十五岁，弃银行而作曲，住左岸 118 rue de Grenelle；1881 年 9 月三坐 Renoir；1903 年死于常规手术并发症，年五十七；据 Jean Renoir 所述与 Renoir 为友。
Raoul Montefiore——伊琳娜的表亲兼邻居，年龄几乎相同，自认是她最好的童年玩伴；回忆写在躲盖世太保期间，妻送奥斯维辛，文稿被纳粹抄走。
Charles Ephrussi——敖德萨犹太粮食银行继承人、艺术评论家、藏家，卡昂当尔夫妇的艺术顾问；被 Renoir 画进《船上的午宴》一角，亦是 Proust 笔下 Charles Swan 的素材。
Ignace Ephrussi——夏尔之兄，同桌 1880 年 7 月 31 日之餐；Fanny Ephrussi——夏尔之妹，1880 年 8 月记述 Renoir 催画 Alice 之信。
Charles Deudon——矿业继承人、藏家，Renoir 的推手与密友；Renoir 抱怨付款一事即写信给他。
Marguerite Charpentier——出版商之妻、女沙龙主人，Renoir 的赞助人，1879 年沙龙为其画游说评审。
Pierre-Auguste Renoir——画家，本章另一主角；工匠出身（父辈 tailor、seamstress，祖父 shoemaker，兄弟 silversmith），画瓷学徒出身；其子 Jean Renoir 为电影导演（多次入画的童模），兄弟 Edmond Renoir；住址 35 rue St.-Georges。
Monsieur Rousseau——伊琳娜的私人教师，1870 年普法战争与巴黎公社旧伤，随身带左轮手枪与 20 法郎。
Gilbert Cahen d’Anvers——伊琳娜之侄；其妻 Josefina 于 2025 年在巴黎十六区受访，转述亡夫关于双人像才真正惹恼祖辈、以及 Renoir 来访时把画请下楼的记忆。
Georges Hérelle——哲学教授，Albert 密友与同游者，Belle Époque 同性恋史的记录者，文稿藏特鲁瓦 Médiathèque Jacques-Chirac。
John Singer Sargent——25 岁获 1881 年沙龙二等勋章（Mme. Ramón Subercaseaux 像）；Marie-Louise Pailleron（九岁，后称坐像为「catastrophe」）与其父、诗人剧作家 Édouard Pailleron 为同年竞争者。

旁及：Émile Zola（1876 年称肖像画为「历史画的小零钱」）、Camille Pissarro、Edgar Degas、Léon Bonnat、Carolus-Duran、Ambroise Vollard（Renoir 长期画商）、Paul Durand-Ruel（画商）、Henri Cernuschi（引见之地的主人）、Paul Cézanne、Marcel Proust、Henry Havard（保守评论家）、Ernesta Stern（Trieste 沙龙女主人）。
